newsitem.title: NORWAY: Christiania says H1 profit satisfactory.
newsitem.headline: Christiania says H1 profit satisfactory.

text.p: Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, Norway's second largest bank, on Wednesday announced a six-month net profit of 1,210 million crowns, up from 1,099 million in the corresponding 1996 period.
Earnings per share amounted to 2.20 crowns, a rise of 0.20 crowns.
Net profit in the second quarter amounted to 525 million crowns, down from 544 million.

"The six-month net profit corresponds to a satisfactory return on equity of 24 per cent, annualized, among other things as a result of low taxes and negative loan losses," Christiania said in a statement.
Christiania president and CEO Tom Ruud said: "The net profit is at a satisfactory level, but strong competition has put further pressure on interest rate margins.
"We will put priority on profitability rather than volumes and focus on maintaining healthy margins," he said.
"The strong loan growth this quarter is a result of special circumstances and is not representative of future development," Ruud added.
Operating profit before loan losses and profit on long-term securities in the second quarter totalled 458 million crowns, down from 480 million in the corresponding 1996 period.
On a six-month basis, the figure was 1,050 million crowns, up from 978 million.

"The trend in the bank's costs shows consistency with adopted plans, and costs in the second quarter were higher than in the first quarter and the corresponding period last year, due to investments in new technology," the statement said.
"Net interest income was slightly reduced compared with the previous quarter, which was a particularly good quarter," it said.

"The reduction in net interest income is a result of continued strong competition in the market, and the bank's interest rate reductions to customers in the first quarter did largely not take effect until the second quarter."
For the first half, net interest income rose to 1,737 million crowns from 1,704 million.

Net lending to customers increased by 12.4 billion crowns in the last quarter, of which approximately three billion resulted from increased foreign currency rates. The remaining growth primarily relates to disbursement of new loans to the shipping and oil industries this quarter as a result of the Bank's successful bids for new mandates, the statement said.
"At the end of the quarter the quality of the loan portfolio remained good, in line with that of the previous quarter. At the close of the quarter, total assets were 185.2 billion crowns," it said.
The bank said strategic objectives remained unchanged following the rejection by Storebrand shareholders of the proposed merger between Christiania and the insurance company on June 26.

"The objectives previously communicated to the market by Christiania Bank as an independent bank remain firm, and will form the basis for the Bank's operations and further development," the statement said.
